say.en: News channels often report that "the rupee fell to a record low against the dollar". A dollar is just a currency, yet its price in rupees keeps changing. Who buys and sells dollars in India, and how does the market settle on a price? In this lesson: Define the foreign exchange rate.
Explain the sources of demand for and supply of foreign exchange.
Find the equilibrium rate under a flexible system.

body.en: The *foreign exchange rate* is the price of one unit of foreign currency in terms of domestic currency, for example ₹83 per US dollar. It links the prices of goods across countries. When the rupee price of a dollar rises, the rupee depreciates; when it falls, the rupee appreciates. The real exchange rate compares price levels too: $\text{real rate} = eP_f/P$, where $P_f$ is the foreign price level and P the domestic price level.

title.en: On the board: Demand and supply of dollars

narration.en: The flexible exchange rate is set where the demand for dollars meets the supply of dollars.

say.en: Price of the dollar in rupees is on the vertical axis; dollars traded on the horizontal.
Demand falls as the dollar gets dearer; supply rises. They meet at 80 rupees.
Now imports rise. Demand shifts right and the dollar climbs to 84: the rupee depreciates.
If exports or inflows rise instead, supply shifts right and the rupee appreciates.
The flexible exchange rate is set where the demand for dollars meets the supply of dollars.

title.en: Demand, supply and the flexible exchange rate

body.en: Demand for foreign exchange comes from imports of goods and services, Indians investing or studying or travelling abroad, gifts sent abroad and speculation. It slopes downward: a dearer dollar makes imports costlier. Supply comes from exports, foreign tourists, foreign investment into India and remittances. It slopes upward: a dearer dollar makes Indian goods cheaper abroad, raising exports. Under a flexible (floating) *exchange rate* system the rate settles where demand equals supply, without central bank intervention.

points.en: *Supply*: exports, foreign tourists, foreign investment, remittances

narration.en: Let us work through this together. The demand for dollars is Qd = 500 − 5e and the supply is Qs = 5e − 300 (Q in $ million, e in ₹ per $). (a) Find the equilibrium rate. (b) If demand rises to Qd = 600 − 5e, find the new rate and say what happens to the rupee.

say.en: Let us work through this together. The demand for dollars is Qd equals 500 minus 5e and the supply is Qs equals 5e minus 300 (Q in million, e in ₹ per). a Find the equilibrium rate. b If demand rises to Qd equals 600 minus 5e, find the new rate and say what happens to the rupee.
a 500 minus 5e equals 5e minus 300, so 10e equals 800 and e equals 80 rupees per; Q equals 500 minus 400 equals 100 million.
b 600 minus 5e equals 5e minus 300, so 10e equals 900 and e equals 90 rupees per; Q equals 600 minus 450 equals 150 million.
The dollar now costs more rupees, so the rupee has depreciated.
So the answer is a 80 rupees per b 90 rupees per: the rupee depreciates.

narration.en: Recap. The exchange rate is the price of foreign currency in domestic currency. Demand for dollars comes from imports and investing abroad; it slopes down. Supply of dollars comes from exports and inflows; it slopes up. Under a flexible system the rate is set where demand equals supply.
narration.kn: ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ. ವಿನಿಮಯ ದರ ಎಂದರೆ ದೇಶೀಯ ಕರೆನ್ಸಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ವಿದೇಶಿ ಕರೆನ್ಸಿಯ ಬೆಲೆ. ಡಾಲರ್ ಬೇಡಿಕೆ ಆಮದು ಮತ್ತು ವಿದೇಶಿ ಹೂಡಿಕೆಯಿಂದ; ರೇಖೆ ಕೆಳಮುಖ. ಡಾಲರ್ ಪೂರೈಕೆ ರಫ್ತು ಮತ್ತು ಒಳಹರಿವಿನಿಂದ; ರೇಖೆ ಮೇಲ್ಮುಖ. ನಮ್ಯ ವ್ಯವಸ್ಥೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಬೇಡಿಕೆ = ಪೂರೈಕೆ ಆಗುವಲ್ಲಿ ದರ ನಿರ್ಧಾರ.

title.en: Fixed, flexible and managed floating exchange rates
title.kn: ಸ್ಥಿರ, ನಮ್ಯ ಮತ್ತು ನಿರ್ವಹಿತ ತೇಲುವ ವಿನಿಮಯ ದರಗಳು

say.en: Let us recall the key ideas. The exchange rate is the price of foreign currency in domestic currency.
say.kn: ಮುಖ್ಯ ಅಂಶಗಳನ್ನು ನೆನಪಿಸಿಕೊಳ್ಳೋಣ. ವಿನಿಮಯ ದರ ಎಂದರೆ ದೇಶೀಯ ಕರೆನ್ಸಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ವಿದೇಶಿ ಕರೆನ್ಸಿಯ ಬೆಲೆ.

say.en: Demand for dollars comes from imports and investing abroad; it slopes down.
say.kn: ಡಾಲರ್ ಬೇಡಿಕೆ ಆಮದು ಮತ್ತು ವಿದೇಶಿ ಹೂಡಿಕೆಯಿಂದ; ರೇಖೆ ಕೆಳಮುಖ.

say.en: Supply of dollars comes from exports and inflows; it slopes up.
say.kn: ಡಾಲರ್ ಪೂರೈಕೆ ರಫ್ತು ಮತ್ತು ಒಳಹರಿವಿನಿಂದ; ರೇಖೆ ಮೇಲ್ಮುಖ.

say.en: Under a flexible system the rate is set where demand equals supply.
say.kn: ನಮ್ಯ ವ್ಯವಸ್ಥೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಬೇಡಿಕೆ = ಪೂರೈಕೆ ಆಗುವಲ್ಲಿ ದರ ನಿರ್ಧಾರ.
